source: C. F. C. Chang et al., Nat. Electron. 9, 346 (2026); arXiv:2501.16213v1, Fig. 2a (Delta R_xx, light-hole oscillation) and Fig. 2c (Delta R_xx - Delta R_LH^fit, the heavy-hole oscillation left after subtracting the light-hole fit), both on the same ohm scale.
method: Page 16 of the arXiv PDF rendered with pdf.js at scale 2 (1224 x 1584 px). The 1.8 K and 2.1 K curves were located by their colour; the ohm axis was calibrated on the tick marks (20 Ohm = 31 px, zero of each curve at its labelled offset) and the 1/B axis on its tick marks (0.005 T^-1 = 54 px). In windows one light-hole period wide (light) or two heavy-hole periods wide (heavy) a sinusoid at 166 T or 795 T plus a linear background was fitted by least squares with outlier rejection; the amplitude of the sinusoid is recorded.
validation: A straight-line fit of ln(amplitude) against 1/B to the eleven 1.8 K light-hole amplitudes gives a Dingle mobility of 393 cm^2/Vs, against the reported 368 +/- 14 cm^2/Vs.
resolution: One pixel is 0.65 Ohm; the rms residual of the heavy-hole sinusoid fits is 0.4 to 0.6 Ohm.
used_for_ratio: The ratio A_H / A_L is formed at 1/B = 0.0150, 0.0158 and 0.0166 T^-1 (66.7, 63.3 and 60.2 T), where the heavy-hole amplitude is at least three times the fit residual; the light-hole amplitude at 0.0158 T^-1 at 1.8 K is interpolated between 0.0150 and 0.0165.
